summary: This change prevents `astro check` from hanging by closing stdin and setting CI environment variables, while also preferring the project-local Astro binary to avoid the interactive install prompt.

pr_summary.headline: This change prevents `astro check` from hanging by closing stdin and setting CI environment variables, while also preferring the project-local Astro binary to avoid the interactive install prompt.

walkthrough.text: `base.py` threads an optional `stdin: int | None` parameter through `_run_subprocess` → `_run_subprocess_result` → `run_subprocess`, and `subprocess_executor.py` passes it to `subprocess.run`, defaulting to `None` to preserve existing behavior.
`_local_astro_binary` is added to return `node_modules/.bin/astro` (or `astro.cmd` on Windows) when present, using only `is_file()` without an executability check on POSIX.
`_get_astro_command` is extended with an optional `cwd` parameter and now prefers the local binary before falling back to global `astro`, `bunx`, or `npx`.

In `check()`, `get_subprocess_env()` is called (returns an os.environ copy), augmented with `CI=1` and `ASTRO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`, and passed alongside `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` to `_run_subprocess`; a timeout now logs the closed-stdin context.

Nine regression tests are added, all mocking `_run_subprocess` at the plugin level to capture kwargs and assert correct env and stdin wiring — without covering the forwarding chain below that boundary.

verdict_reasoning.deciding_factor: No P1 issues block the merge. The most significant gap is a P2: all nine regression tests mock `_run_subprocess` (a private plugin method), so the critical `stdin=DEVNULL` and `env` values are verified only at the top of the call stack. The chain through `base.py:_run_subprocess_result` → `subprocess_executor.py:run_subprocess` → `subprocess.run` is unexercised, and `tests/unit/plugins/base/test_subprocess.py` contains zero stdin coverage. A future refactor that accidentally drops `stdin` from that chain would not be caught by any test, meaning issue #940 could silently recur in production.
verdict_reasoning.failure_mechanism: If `_run_subprocess_result` were modified to call `run_subprocess(cmd, effective_timeout, cwd, env)` — omitting `stdin` — `subprocess.run` would receive `stdin=None` (inherit parent), the interactive `@astrojs/check` install prompt would block again, and the plugin would time out as before. The astro-check unit tests would still pass because they intercept at `_run_subprocess` before the forwarding chain runs.

file_assessments.overview: Adds an optional `stdin` parameter to `_run_subprocess` and `_run_subprocess_result`, threading it positionally through to `run_subprocess`.
Adds an optional `stdin` parameter to `run_subprocess` and passes it directly to `subprocess.run`, after merging `env` with os.environ.

Adds `_local_astro_binary` for local binary discovery (is_file() only), updates command building to prefer it, and forces non-interactive execution via CI=1, ASTRO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1, and stdin=DEVNULL.
Adds nine regression tests for non-interactive behavior, local binary preference, Windows handling, fallback logic, and timeout handling, all mocking at the `_run_subprocess` private-method boundary.

findings.title: stdin/env forwarding chain below _run_subprocess is untested
findings.description: All nine regression tests for issue #940 mock `_run_subprocess` and verify that `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` and `env['CI']='1'` are passed to it. But the fix depends on those values reaching `subprocess.run` three call frames deeper. The forwarding chain `_run_subprocess_result → run_subprocess → subprocess.run` has no test coverage anywhere: `tests/unit/plugins/base/test_subprocess.py` contains zero `stdin` assertions, and no other test file exercises it. A silent regression dropping `stdin` in that chain would cause issue #940 to recur without any failing test.
findings.cause: Tests anchor at the plugin's private `_run_subprocess` method, but the observable behavior that fixes #940 — `subprocess.run` receiving `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` — lives in `base.py:_run_subprocess_result` and `subprocess_executor.py:run_subprocess`, neither of which received new tests in this PR.
findings.fix: Add a test in `tests/unit/plugins/base/test_subprocess.py` that calls `_run_subprocess_result(cmd, timeout, cwd, env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)` on a concrete plugin instance and asserts `subprocess.run` is called with `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` (patch `subprocess.run` directly). Alternatively, replace one of the existing astro-check tests with a version that patches `subprocess.run` instead of `_run_subprocess`, verifying end-to-end that stdin=DEVNULL survives the full call stack.

findings.title: Non-executable local shim causes PermissionError not graceful fallback
findings.description: On non-Windows, `_local_astro_binary` returns any path that satisfies `is_file()`, including files without execute permission. If `node_modules/.bin/astro` exists but lacks the execute bit (e.g., a corrupted install, a freshly-extracted tarball, or a manually placed placeholder), `subprocess.run` raises `PermissionError` rather than falling back to the global `astro` or `bunx`/`npx`. The function's own docstring promises 'an executable project-local binary', but the implementation does not enforce that on POSIX.
findings.cause: `shim if shim.is_file() else None` (line 78) omits `os.access(shim, os.X_OK)` on the POSIX branch. The Windows branch has no equivalent problem because `.cmd` files are invoked via `cmd.exe` which does not require the execute bit.
findings.fix: Add an executability check on the POSIX branch: `return shim if shim.is_file() and os.access(shim, os.X_OK) else None`. This also requires adding `import os` to the file's imports.
findings.suggested_code:
shim = bin_dir / "astro"
    return shim if shim.is_file() and os.access(shim, os.X_OK) else None

findings.title: Regression tests coupled to private method _run_subprocess
findings.description: Seven of the nine new tests use `patch.object(astro_check_plugin, '_run_subprocess', side_effect=capture)`. If `_run_subprocess` is renamed, or if the call site in `check()` is refactored to call `_run_subprocess_result` directly (both are valid internal changes), all seven mocks silently stop intercepting anything. The tests would still pass — `capture` would never be called, `captured` would remain empty — and the real subprocess call would fire against the system, producing an error unrelated to the behavior under test.
findings.cause: Tests assert on kwargs passed to a private implementation method rather than to a stable observable boundary (the tool result, a public API, or `subprocess.run`).
findings.fix: Document the intentional mock boundary in a module-level comment (cheapest), or move the mock target to `subprocess.run` / `run_subprocess` so that the tests survive internal plugin refactors without silently losing coverage.
